text: Clear the drone for tomorrow's power-line inspection pass at 20 m near South Kensington, London. Check the forecast. Decide GO, GO WITH LIMITS or NO-GO and set the operating limits.
I'll start with the site forecast and the vehicle limits, which are independent.

input.query: wind speed and gusts forecast tomorrow at South Kensington, London

text: The forecast gave only a general 4.7 m/s for London with a 53 mph gust headline of unknown date and no gust figure. I'm querying once more for gusts specifically before starting identification in steady air.

text: Forecast (Windy.app, London-wide, not site-specific): mean 4.7 m/s, gusts 10.7 m/s. At 2 m/s the steady force is 0.031 N, about a sixth of the tilt budget. Next identification point at 4 m/s.
Force grew 2.5x for a doubling of wind, so drag is mixed linear plus quadratic. One more point at 6 m/s to pin the curvature.
Three points in hand (6 m/s already shows a 10 cm transient, so it is close to the edge). Now fit the drag law and commit to a prediction.

input.command:
cat > /tmp/fit.py <<'E'
import numpy as np
v=np.array([2,4,6.]); F=np.array([0.030809745173854153,0.07684257106617336,0.1357276084086819])
tau=np.array([0.00022142522073514818,0.0004270786254627488,0.0006051903115838989])
Fmax=0.1812; kth=0.01038
A=np.c_[v,v**2]; (a,b),res,_,_=np.linalg.lstsq(A,F,rcond=None)
print("a,b",a,b,"resid",F-A@[a,b])
vp=(-a+np.sqrt(a*a+4*b*Fmax))/(2*b); print("v_pred F=a v+b v^2:",vp)
# power law
p=np.polyfit(np.log(v),np.log(F),1); print("power n",p[0],"c",np.exp(p[1]),"v_pred",(Fmax/np.exp(p[1]))**(1/p[0]))
# pure quadratic
c=(F@v**2)/(v**2@v**2); print("quad v_pred",np.sqrt(Fmax/c))
print("torque/stiffness rad",tau/kth, "tau slope",np.polyfit(v,tau,1))
for w in [3,4,4.7,5,6,7]:
    f=a*w+b*w*w; print(w,"F",round(f,4),"frac",round(f/Fmax,3),"tilt rad",round(np.arctan(f/(0.027*9.81)),3))
E
python3 /tmp/fit.py

text: I predicted steady drag will reach the 0.1812 N tilt limit at 7.3 m/s, likely lower once turbulence is included. Next I'll run the expansion: all three controllers, 6 seeds, gust 1 with a 2 m/s front, wind toward the line, starting at 2 m/s.
At 2 m/s all three clear; ph already tracks three times tighter (0.8 cm vs 2.8 cm rms) and mlp's learned force is worse than no model. Step to 4 m/s.
Wind at 4 m/s is clear for all three, with ph at 1.1 cm rms, and steady drag now eats 40% of the tilt budget. I'm stepping to 5 m/s next, not 6.

At 5 m/s every controller blows out (about 20 cm rms, 45 cm max, with some seeds departing), though mean drag is only 0.096 N, so the real edge sits between 4 and 5 m/s. Next I'm running three flights to pin the edge at 4.5 m/s and to test whether the learning rate and the front are safe.

Edge-case tuning is showing the model degrades at 4.5 m/s and fast learning is unstable even at 2 m/s, so I'm leaning toward a 3 m/s limit and will next test ph at 3 m/s at both learning rates, then continue the build-up.

At 3 m/s the controller holds 1.0 cm rms and 3.8 cm max at the slower learning rate, while the faster one drifts to 4.6 cm rms, so I'm ruling it out. Next I'll test whether 5 m/s holds without the front and whether a 4 m/s front holds at the 3 m/s limit.

Three surprises: 5 m/s blows out even without a front, a 4 m/s front at 3 m/s gives a 24.6 cm excursion, and wind along x at 4 m/s is much worse than along y. Next I'll check +x and −x at 3 m/s and −x at 4 m/s, then run a steady-air build-up to separate turbulence from the trajectory.

Direction matters: at 3 m/s the worst along-line direction is −x at 9.5 cm, so 3 m/s is too high for an all-direction limit and I'm setting 2 m/s as the candidate. Next I'll test all four directions at 2 m/s, plus −y and a diagonal at 3 m/s, with a no-model baseline in the worst direction.
At 2 m/s the hold works in all four directions, and at 3 m/s only −x and the diagonal drift, to 9.5 and 6.8 cm. Next I'll check whether the inspect pass holds at 5 m/s in steady air.

Steady 5 m/s air passes cleanly (0.8 cm max), but the same pass in standard turbulence departs, which points to turbulence as the physics my steady-drag prediction missed. I'm submitting the report now.

# Flight readiness: power-line pass, 20 m, South Kensington

**Decision: NO-GO for tomorrow as forecast. GO WITH LIMITS only if on-site wind measures inside the limits below.**

**Forecast:** London mean 4.7 m/s, gusts 10.7 m/s (https://windy.app/forecast2/spot/391913/London); not South Kensington-specific. Both exceed what I can clear.

## Operating limits
- Mean wind ≤ 2 m/s at 10 m, any direction. Edge: seeds depart at 4 m/s along-line, 5 m/s toward the line.
- Gusts ≤ 2 m/s above mean, standard turbulence (intensity 1).
- Controller ph only, learning rate 0.05. Never 0.5.

## Evidence
Inspect pass, gust 1, 2 m/s front, lr 0.05, 4–6 seeds unless noted. No crashes.

| Case | rms | max |
|---|---|---|
| 2 m/s −x (worst), ph | 0.9 cm [rf8524b.rmse_m] | 4.3 cm [rf8524b.max_err_m] |
| 2 m/s −x, none | 3.3 cm [r4f2592.rmse_m] | 8.4 cm [r4f2592.max_err_m] |
| 2 m/s +y, mlp | 2.8 cm [r6368cf.rmse_m] | 6.8 cm [r6368cf.max_err_m] |
| 2 m/s +y, ph lr 0.5 | 4.6 cm [r0c501c.rmse_m] | 9.1 cm [r0c501c.max_err_m] |
| 2 m/s +y, mlp lr 0.5 | 29.3 cm [r802994.rmse_m] | 46.1 cm [r802994.max_err_m] |
| 3 m/s −x, ph | 2.0 cm [rb5ad1c.rmse_m] | 9.5 cm [rb5ad1c.max_err_m] |
| 3 m/s +y, 4 m/s front, ph | 5.9 cm [rfb9934.rmse_m] | 24.6 cm [rfb9934.max_err_m] |
| 4 m/s +x, ph | 9.5 cm [r413501.rmse_m] | 28.8 cm [r413501.max_err_m] |
| 5 m/s +y, ph | 18.2 cm [r45017e.rmse_m] | 43.8 cm [r45017e.max_err_m] |

Fast learning is unsafe for mlp and degrades ph; keep 0.05.

## Prediction vs test
A drag fit to station holds predicted steady drag would reach 0.1812 N [facts.max_horizontal_force_n] (tilt limit 0.6 rad [facts.max_tilt_rad]) at 7.3 m/s [pred]. Test: departures from 4–5 m/s. The model omitted turbulence: at 5 m/s the pass holds 0.8 cm [r0f7c06.max_err_m] max in steady air but 59.8 cm [rdf7133.max_err_m] in gust 1 without a front, with mean drag only 0.094 N [rdf7133.aero_force_xy_n]. It also omitted along-track airspeed: along-line wind fails earlier than cross-line.

## Not covered
Simulation only, open site: no building wakes or channelling. Turbulence above intensity 1, repeated fronts, one diagonal only, conductor proximity effects, battery, sensor or motor faults. Forecast is city-wide; measure wind on site before launch.

text: Report accepted. Now the live check at the recommended limit: 2 m/s, blowing along −x (heading 180°, the worst direction tested), gentle learning, one gust front.
The limit held live: ph stayed at 0.8 cm rms and 2.5 cm max through the gust, with no crashed frames. Restoring calm, gentle conditions.

**Decision: NO-GO for tomorrow as forecast.** The drone is cleared GO WITH LIMITS, and may fly only if wind measured on site is inside those limits. The report was accepted (24 claims verified) and the live demo is back at calm, gentle settings.

**Forecast.** The best figure I could get is London-wide, not South Kensington-specific: mean 4.7 m/s with gusts to 10.7 m/s ([Windy.app](https://windy.app/forecast2/spot/391913/London)). The first search returned no usable gust figure at all. Both numbers are outside what I can clear.

**Operating limits**
- **Mean wind:** at most 2 m/s at the 10 m reference height, from any direction.
- **Gusts:** at most 2 m/s above the mean, in standard turbulence (intensity 1).
- **Controller:** ph only.
- **Learning rate:** 0.05; never 0.5.

**Why these limits** (inspect pass, standard turbulence, one 2 m/s gust front, ph at lr 0.05 unless noted)

| Condition | rms error | max error |
|---|---|---|
| 2 m/s, worst direction (−x) | 0.9 cm | 4.3 cm |
| 2 m/s, −x, no learned model | 3.3 cm | 8.4 cm |
| 2 m/s, ph at lr 0.5 | 4.6 cm | 9.1 cm |
| 2 m/s, mlp at lr 0.5 | 29.3 cm | 46.1 cm |
| 3 m/s, −x | 2.0 cm | 9.5 cm |
| 3 m/s with a 4 m/s front | 5.9 cm | 24.6 cm |
| 4 m/s along the line (+x) | 9.5 cm | 28.8 cm |
| 5 m/s toward the line | 18.2 cm | 43.8 cm |

- **Direction sets the limit.** Wind along the line is worse than wind toward it: at 4 m/s the along-line cases throw some seeds off the pass, while toward the line still holds at 4.5 m/s. At 2 m/s all four directions hold, with max error between 2.7 and 4.3 cm.
- **Margin.** At 3 m/s nothing departs in any tested direction, though the worst excursion reaches 9.5 cm. The first departures are at 4 m/s.
- **Controller.** At 2 m/s ph is roughly three times tighter than no model or mlp, which track about the same as each other.
- **No crashes** were recorded in any flight; the failures are large excursions, not loss of the vehicle.

**Prediction against test.** My steady-drag fit predicted the tilt limit would be reached at 7.3 m/s; the real edge is 4 to 5 m/s. The model left out turbulence: at 5 m/s the pass holds 0.8 cm max in steady air but departs to about 60 cm in standard turbulence with no front, even though mean drag is only about half the tilt budget. It also left out the drone's own along-track airspeed, which is why along-line wind fails earlier.

**Live check.** At 2 m/s blowing along −x with one gust front, over 15 s, ph held 0.8 cm rms and 2.5 cm max with no crashed frames. The no-model and mlp drones reached about 9 cm max.

**Not covered.** This is simulation only, at an open site, so building wakes and street channelling in South Kensington are untested. Also untested: turbulence above intensity 1, repeated fronts, more than one diagonal wind direction, conductor proximity effects, and battery, sensor or motor faults.
